key: As I, remembering thee with grateful spirit, a mortal, call with might on thee Immortal, Vouchsafe us high renown, O Jatavedas, and may I be immortal by my children.
s: Near the end of a hymn that calls Agni father and guest, the singer makes his own plea; Sāyaṇa, on 5.4.10, reads this immortality as a line of descendants never broken, citing a text in which the mortal is born again in his offspring.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.4.10, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 324070 (2021)

evidence.words: हे “जातवेदः “यशः धनं प्रजां वा “अस्मासु “धेहि । "प्रजाभिः त्वद्दत्ताभिर्हे “अग्ने अहम् “अमृतत्वं संतत्यविच्छेदलक्षणम् “अश्यां प्राप्नुयाम् । प्रजामनु प्रजायसे तदु ते मर्त्यामृतम्' (तै. ब्रा. १. ५. ५. ६ ) इति हि श्रुतिः ॥
evidence.gloss: O Jātavedas, place in us renown, that is wealth or offspring. By offspring given by thee, O Agni, may I attain immortality, the kind marked by the unbroken continuance of the line; for scripture says: after offspring thou art born again; that, O mortal, is thy immortality (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 1.5.5.6).

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 5.4.10, at [357,10]). Sāyaṇa on 5.4.10 glosses amṛtatvam as immortality marked by the unbroken continuance of the line (saṃtatyavicchedalakṣaṇam) and cites the śruti prajām anu prajāyase tad u te martyāmṛtam (TB 1.5.5.6), in which the mortal is born again after his offspring; Wilson note 1 reports the same. Plain sense faithful: 5.4.2 calls Agni Eternal Father, 5.4.5 guest in the dwelling, and 5.4.10 is the singer’s own first-person plea in the hymn’s penultimate verse.
